summary: Catalogue-wide screen of 217 active roadmaps including the focal roadmap, independently spot-checked against 2007 stage records. Ten prerequisite links: the original seven IntegralLattices inputs and two FF.4 outputs, plus the reviewer-added orthogonal-lattice-sum input to coding Layer 7. Three scoped overlaps preserve coordinate-power reuse, common finite Fourier foundations and the unresolved GN.4 lattice-code handoff. Baseline constructors are reuse inputs; code-specific comparisons and consumer proof obligations remain open.

provenance.note: Authorized GitHub Pages artifact supplied the scratch input tree. Commit comparison showed only unrelated audit24/audit25/queue/ledger changes from the input revision. All physical roadmap documents match atlas readme strings. No git commands were run.

screen.method: Read all summaries, search every full README/title/stage description for nine focal-object families plus four wider synonym families, then read all selected supplier/consumer stages in full. Detailed reading is not claimed for every unrelated proof. New roadmap definitions, completed upstream roadmaps, all same-area roadmaps, neighboring areas and existing link packets were included.

screen.confidencePolicy: explicit follows the job-specific rule: a text names the other roadmap/stage; both endpoint outputs/uses are quoted. The integral-lattice dependency is also named reciprocally in the two scope sections. FF.4 explicitly names AlgebraicCodingTheory. No inference from terminology alone.

links.reason: IntegralLattices supplies the embedded rational integral-lattice object, form and isometry vocabulary used to bundle Construction A. For m >= 2, coding must first prove fullness of the inverse-image carrier with B_m = dot/m and self-orthogonality before supplying integrality. This is reuse of the supplier, not permission to bundle an arbitrary nonintegral code preimage as IntegralLattice.

evidence.quote:
Define an integral symmetric lattice from a carrier `L : Submodule ℤ V` with
  `[L.IsLattice ℚ]`, a symmetric `B : BilinForm ℚ V`, and a proof that `B(L,L)⊆ℤ`.
  Supply coercions to the carrier and form, an extensionality theorem, access to a carrier basis and
  rank, and constructors from a basis plus an integral symmetric Gram matrix and from an
  existing full submodule with form.

Prove that `P_m(C)` is a full `ℤ`-lattice in `ℚ^ι` for every `C`.  It bundles as an
  `IntegralLattice` exactly when `C ≤ C^⊥`.

links.reason: The dual carrier, discriminant and equivalent unimodularity criteria are the lattice interfaces used by the integral Construction-A application. Nondegeneracy of dot/m follows from m >= 2, but integrality still requires C <= C-perp. The stronger literal dual identity for arbitrary additive C is coding-owned elementary residue pairing; this edge does not assert that the integral-lattice theorem proves that identity for a nonintegral carrier.

evidence.quote:
Prove the equivalence of the following, with nondegeneracy, integrality, fullness, and finite rank
  visible in the theorem context: `L=L^∨`; `A_L` is trivial; `#A_L=1`; the Gram determinant has
  absolute value one; and the restricted pairing `L → Module.Dual ℤ L` is an equivalence.  Signed
  determinant `-1` is allowed.

Prove that integral `P_m(C)` is unimodular exactly when `C=C^⊥`.  Keep self-orthogonality visible
  in the construction so “unimodular” is never asserted of an unbundled nonintegral carrier.

links.reason: The additive-code branch explicitly imports a finite bilinear alphabet from IntegralLattices. Its summed coordinate pairing and quadratic refinement use that finite-form carrier, perpendicular operation and nondegenerate cardinality/double-perpendicular API. Do not confuse a finite Q/Z-valued alphabet with an arbitrary field-valued Hermitian space. Coordinate powers themselves already have the checked pinned Tau Ceti APIs listed below.

evidence.quote:
Define the radical, isotropic elements and subgroups, `H^⊥`, and Lagrangians.  Prove
  `H ≤ H^⊥` under the appropriate bilinear-isotropy hypothesis and under quadratic isotropy, the
  unconditional inclusion `H ≤ H^⊥⊥`, order reversal, and the general finite formula
  `H^⊥⊥ = H + rad(b)`.  Deduce the double-perp equality `H^⊥⊥=H` and
  `|H| |H^⊥| = |A|` only under nondegeneracy.  Deduce `|H|²=|A|` for a Lagrangian.  Provide
  explicit membership and computation lemmas, rather than exposing these notions only through the
  later correspondence.

For a finite bilinear alphabet `A` from the integral-lattices roadmap, construct the coordinate
  power on `ι → A` by summing pairings.  Define the orthogonal additive code and prove the
  finite-cardinality and double-perpendicular results under nondegeneracy.  Construct the analogous
  coordinate finite quadratic module by summing quadratic values.

links.reason: The construction of the L0 = m Z^i discriminant coordinate map consumes the literal dual/subtype-quotient discriminant carrier and its quotient map. Coding must prove L0-dual = Z^i and that reduction modulo m induces the displayed isometry; neither an abstract group of the right order nor an opaque equivalence replaces this comparison. m >= 2 is inherited from Construction A.

evidence.quote:
Define `A_L` as the actual quotient of the subtype `L^∨` by the inverse-image of `L`; provide its
  quotient map, representative lemmas, zero criterion, additive-group structure, and functorial map
  induced by an isometry.  Prove it finite using equal rank and Mathlib's finite-quotient API.

Let `L₀(m,ι)` have carrier `mℤ^ι` in `ℚ^ι` and form `B_m`.  Prove
  `L₀(m,ι)^∨=ℤ^ι` and construct an isometry
  `A_{L₀} ≅ (ZMod m)^ι` carrying the class of an integer vector to its coordinatewise
  reduction modulo `m`, and carrying the discriminant pairing to
  `∑ lift(x_i)lift(y_i)/m mod ℤ`.  For even `m`, identify the half-norm quadratic form with `q_m`.

links.reason: Coding transports actual additive subgroups through finite bilinear/quadratic isometries and matches polar forms and perpendiculars. It consumes IntegralLattices finite-form isometries and orthogonal sums, in the Q/Z half-norm convention. The alphabet-to-lattice discriminant comparison and trace-Hermitian F4 coordinate calculation remain coding targets; an additive equivalence without form preservation is insufficient.

evidence.quote:
Define a finite quadratic module by reusing
  `QuadraticMap ℤ A (AddCircle (1 : ℚ))`, and identify its symmetric biadditive polar form
  `b_q(x,y)=q(x+y)-q(x)-q(y)` with the underlying pairing.  Supply morphisms, isometries,
  orthogonal sums, negation, restriction, and passage to the underlying bilinear module.  State
  nondegeneracy through the polar form.  The codomain is the additive quotient `ℚ/ℤ`, not a ring;
  do not introduce a parallel private quadratic-map structure.

State the reusable interface for an isometry from a coordinate finite quadratic module to the
  discriminant module of an orthogonal lattice sum.  Its input subgroup remains an
  `AddSubgroup`; field-linearity is used only when separately proved for a named code.

links.reason: Apply the general intermediate-overlattice/isotropic-subgroup construction and natural discriminant isometry A_(L_H) = H-perp/H after identifying the code with an actual subgroup of A_L0. Bilinear isotropy gives integral gluing; the quadratic refinement additionally requires even m and q_m vanishing on C. Preserve the subtype quotient, representative maps and half-norm convention rather than re-proving gluing or substituting a cardinality equality.

evidence.quote:
For isotropic `H`, define the induced form on `H^⊥/H` and construct the natural isometry
  `A_{L_H} ≅ H^⊥/H`, bilinear in the integral case and quadratic in the even case.  Include the
  representative formula, nondegeneracy, order computation, and compatibility with the index and
  determinant formulae.  Deduce that an even overlattice `L_H` is unimodular exactly when
  `H=H^⊥`, that is, exactly when `H` is Lagrangian.

Consume the general gluing theorem to obtain, for isotropic `C`, the natural isometry
  `A_{P_m(C)} ≅ C^⊥/C`, first as an isometry of finite bilinear modules and, when `m` is even
  and `q_m|_C=0`, as an isometry of finite quadratic modules.  Its underlying quotient must be the
  actual subtype quotient built from `C ≤ C^⊥`; a cardinality equality is not a substitute.
  Deduce unimodularity from the Lagrangian condition `C=C^⊥`, not from an unexplained determinant
  computation.

links.reason: The A_n and D_n discriminant forms specialize at n = 2 and n = 4 to the alphabets used by the tetracode, ternary Golay and hexacode applications. Coding must pin the additive F3/F4 identifications and transport their quadratic values, not import only determinant orders. A2 has q(a) = a^2/3; D4 has q = 1/2 on each nonzero class. General ADE/root classification is supplied transitively through IntegralLattices, not a new direct coding prerequisite.

evidence.quote:
| `A_n`, `n≥1` | `ℤ/(n+1)` | the class of the first fundamental weight generates and has `q=n/(2(n+1))` |
| `D_n`, odd `n≥5` | `ℤ/4` | either spinor class generates; `q(s)=n/8`; the vector class is `2s` and has `q(v)=1/2` |
| `D_n`, even `n≥4` | `(ℤ/2)²` | vector and the two spinor classes are the three nonzero classes; `q(v)=1/2` and `q(s)=q(c)=n/8` |

Verify that the tetracode and `G₁₂` become quadratic-isotropic, Lagrangian subgroups for the
  standard `A₂` discriminant alphabet.  Pin its generator so that, for `a,b∈F₃`,
  `q_A₂(a)=a²/3 mod ℤ` and `b_A₂(a,b)=2ab/3 mod ℤ`.
  Identify the standard `D₄` alphabet additively with `F₄` by sending
  `1` to the vector class and `ω,ω²` to the two spinor classes.

links.reason: FF.4 explicitly connects its evaluation/residue and BCH/Reed-Solomon examples to AlgebraicCodingTheory. Consume the generic finite-coordinate code and generator/check presentation API, with encoding membership and rank/dimension theorems, rather than defining another code carrier. FF.4 owns those code families and their field-size/length restrictions; this edge does not put decoding or algebraic-geometry code construction into the focal roadmap.

evidence.quote:
Define the code generated by a matrix as `range G.vecMulLinear` and the code checked by a matrix
  as `ker H.mulVecLin`.  Define generator- and parity-check-matrix predicates by equality to those
  submodules.  Prove existence from finite bases, the row-span and syndrome membership criteria,
  the rank/dimension formulae, deletion of dependent rows, and invariance under invertible row
  operations.
Develop Galois rings, additive polynomials, permutation polynomials and sequence correlation; connect evaluation/residue codes to existing AlgebraicCodingTheory and AlgebraicCurves.

links.reason: FF.4 requires proved distance bounds for its code families; these use the focal minimum-distance definition and elementary Hamming/coordinate-operation interface. Preserve the zero-code convention and the nonzero-shortening hypothesis. This is not a prerequisite on the entire Hermitian-dual or exceptional-code developments, and FF.4 must prove the family-specific BCH/Reed-Solomon bounds itself.

evidence.quote:
Define minimum distance for linear and additive codes with the zero-code convention above.  For a
  nonzero code, prove attainment by a nonzero word and equality with the least pairwise distance.
  Prove invariance under Hamming isometries and the sharp deleted-coordinate bound for puncturing.
Encoding maps, dimension and distance bounds are proved; BCH/Reed-Solomon examples include field-size and length restrictions.
connect evaluation/residue codes to existing AlgebraicCodingTheory and AlgebraicCurves.

links.reason: Reuse IntegralLattices Layer 1 orthogonal lattice sums and their canonical inclusions/projections and associativity/commutativity isometries for the actual orthogonal lattice sum in the Layer 7 alphabet/discriminant interface. This supplies the lattice-side sum object; Layer 3 supplies the separate finite-form sum. The code owner must still construct any finite-family iteration, the coordinate-power/discriminant isometry, and the named A2/F3 and D4/F4 identifications. A binary sum API is not already an arbitrary finite-family discriminant comparison. This is an ownership/reuse dependency, not a request to rebuild library constructions.

evidence.quote: Construct form scaling, form negation, and orthogonal direct sums.

State the reusable interface for an isometry from a coordinate finite quadratic module to the
  discriminant module of an orthogonal lattice sum.

overlaps.detail: Finite-form orthogonal sums/perpendiculars in IntegralLattices and the coordinate-power work in coding Layers 2 and 7 meet at the same generic finite-alphabet API. Moreover, the pinned Tau Ceti source already constructs both bilinear and quadratic coordinate powers and their coordinatewise isometries, so neither coding layer should rebuild them.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the general finite-form carrier, perpendicular and isometry API with IntegralLattices. Replace the repeated coding construction instructions by imports of the checked coordinatePower, nondegeneracy, membership and coordinatewise-isometry declarations. Coding retains the named alphabet identifications, the Hermitian-to-trace pairing comparison, and the actual discriminant-coordinate maps. No whole-roadmap merge.

evidence.quote:
For a finite bilinear alphabet `A` from the integral-lattices roadmap, construct the coordinate
  power on `ι → A` by summing pairings.  Define the orthogonal additive code and prove the
  finite-cardinality and double-perpendicular results under nondegeneracy.  Construct the analogous
  coordinate finite quadratic module by summing quadratic values.
Build finite coordinate powers and coordinatewise isometries for other discriminant alphabets.

Define a finite quadratic module by reusing
  `QuadraticMap ℤ A (AddCircle (1 : ℚ))`, and identify its symmetric biadditive polar form
  `b_q(x,y)=q(x+y)-q(x)-q(y)` with the underlying pairing.  Supply morphisms, isometries,

overlaps.detail: These stages share the finite additive-character/Fourier orthogonality kernel. The coding text explicitly imports Mathlib primitive characters and nontrivial-character vanishing, while FF.1 and AC.0 describe broader finite-character and Fourier developments. The texts do not establish that coding must await either complete campaign stage.
overlaps.proposal: Reuse the pinned character primitives, choose one common finite-Fourier normalization, and expose the subspace-indicator transform from coding as reusable API. Keep MacWilliams and Krawtchouk coefficients in coding, Gauss/Jacobi sums in FF.1, and convolution/energy and additive-combinatorial inequalities in AC.0. Do not add a dependency arrow merely because all three use characters. Resolve any duplicated general Fourier helper at declaration level.

evidence.quote:
Establish the finite-character orthogonality lemma for a linear subspace and its Euclidean dual.
  Reuse Mathlib's primitive additive character on a finite field and its nontrivial-character sum;
  expose the resulting finite Fourier transform lemma as reusable API rather than burying it in the
  final polynomial calculation.
Construct additive and multiplicative characters, orthogonality, Gauss and Jacobi sums and their norm/product identities; extend zero values consistently.
Build sumsets, additive energy, convolution and Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups; prove basic Plunnecke/Ruzsa and energy inequalities with cardinality assumptions.

overlaps.detail: GN.4 promises to connect lattice codes through FF.4, but FF.4 specifies finite code families and no finite-code-to-real-lattice construction. Construction A is the explicit code/lattice construction in coding Layer 6. The phrase lattice codes is too unspecific to determine a mandatory direct stage edge.
overlaps.proposal: GN.4 should name the actual code/lattice construction it uses. For a Construction-A application, import the coding construction, prove the scalar-extension isometry from the rational carrier with dot/m to the real m^(-1/2) realization, and state the norm/covolume or packing interface needed. FF.4 remains the owner of BCH/Reed-Solomon/evaluation/residue families. Until that use is specified, retain this as an unresolved scope handoff rather than an invented prerequisite or a merge.

evidence.quote: connect lattice codes through FF.4.
Encoding maps, dimension and distance bounds are proved; BCH/Reed-Solomon examples include field-size and length restrictions.

Let `m ≥ 2` and let `C ≤ (ZMod m)^ι` be an additive code.  Define its standard dual by the
`ZMod m` dot product and construct `P_m(C)` and `B_m` using the standing convention.
